page: Google Cloud Platform ct5lp-hightpu-4t is an accelerator-focused server belonging to the ct5lp family. It is built on the x86_64 CPU architecture and features 112 dedicated vCPUs alongside 192.0 GB of system memory. This configuration results in a memory-to-core ratio of 1.71 GB per vCPU. The primary computational capacity is driven by four integrated Google TPU v5e accelerators, which provide a combined total of 64 GB of VRAM.

This server does not include local storage, meaning all data persistence must be managed through external network-attached storage solutions. Additionally, the configuration offers zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses. The low system memory allocation relative to the high vCPU count represents a specific architectural tradeoff, prioritizing host-side coordination and offloading heavy tensor computations directly to the TPU accelerators.

The hardware profile is designed for machine learning workloads, including model training, fine-tuning, and inference. From a qualitative cost-efficiency perspective, the server maximizes accelerator density relative to host resources, minimizing CPU overhead during intensive parallel processing tasks. This makes it a structured choice for workloads that rely heavily on TPU acceleration rather than general-purpose CPU or memory capacity.
